newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr rises vs yen but gains limited by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rises vs yen but gains limited by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0645 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar rose against the yen by late Tokyo on Wednesday, but its gains were limited amid a lack of follow-through purchases due to a dearth of fresh trading incentives, dealers said.
Mark/yen remained top-heavy as the mark's undertone stays weak amid a growing perception of a weak, broad-based euro, which indirectly weighed on dollar/yen, they added.

Investment trust management firms and trust banks were said to be keen to buy dollar on dips, keeping the dollar's downside solid. Interbank dealers also bought back dollars after overnight dips below 115 yen.
"But the dollar's rise was capped as the mark's topside was heavy against the yen," a city bank dealer said.
Short-covering of mark/yen following a sharp dip below 63 yen overnight pushed the mark slightly higher in the morning.
But sporadic exporter sales and steady selling interest on the upside kept the mark below 63.50 yen for most of Tokyo trading.

But a dealer at a different city bank said that some exporters missed out a chance to sell marks against the yen because the mark's fall overnight was too rapid. Meanwhile, another city bank dealer another downside test below 63 yen was still in sight. The German currency stood at 63.41/44 yen at 0715 GMT, compared with 63.31 yen in early Tokyo trading.

Dealers expect the mark to keep weakening against major currencies after soft-euro expectations were further fuelled by overnight comments by Bundesbank member Hans-Juergen Koebnick that the euro could be stable even if France and Germany had deficit/GDP ratios of 3.2-3.3 percent.

"I see a change in the Bundesbank's attitude (towards the EMU). They used to talk about a strong mark and euro, but they now say the euro will be stable even if EMU begins under looser criteria," said Ryosuke Tsuji, senior vice president and manager of the spot forex department at Societe Generale in Tokyo.

A trader at another city bank said: "Buba officials so far have failed to show strong determination to stop the mark's fall. Some players suspect that Buba might be willing to tolerate the dollar/mark's rise to around 1.85 marks."

Singapore dealers said the dollar remained strong against the mark but that immediate gains would be limited as the market was taking a breather after Tuesday's steep rise following Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks.

In his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, Greenspan told a House Banking subcommittee on Tuesday that U.S. economic growth appeared to be slowing and that he was confident of modest inflation through the end of 1997.
Dealers in Tokyo said they are now focusing on the Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday for possible comments on currencies.
But the first city bank dealer said the meeting was expected to have only a limited impact as it is unlikely there will be a change to German monetary policy.
The dollar closed at 114.95/00 yen and 1.8230/40 marks in New York on Tuesday.
